hints: Consider the entire system of mass $M = 1200 + 800 = 2000\text{ kg}$ to find acceleration $a$.
Parallel equation of motion: $F_D - R_{\text{total}} - Mg\sin\theta = Ma$.
Consider the trailer alone to find the tension $T$: $T - R_{\text{trailer}} - m_{\text{trailer}}g\sin\theta = m_{\text{trailer}}a$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the entire system (car + trailer) up the incline ($M = 1200 + 800 = 2000\text{ kg}$):
$$F_D - (R_{\text{car}} + R_{\text{trailer}}) - Mg\sin\theta = Ma$$
$$2500 - (100 + 150) - 2000(10)(0.1) = 2000a$$
$$2500 - 250 - 2000 = 2000a \implies 250 = 2000a \implies a = \frac{250}{2000} = 0.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Consider the trailer alone ($m = 800\text{ kg}$) to determine the cable tension $T$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} - mg\sin\theta = ma$$
$$T - 150 - 800(10)(0.1) = 800(0.125)$$
$$T - 150 - 800 = 100 \implies T - 950 = 100 \implies T = 1050\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Solving Connected-Particle Systems: Uses $T=1050$ N, obtaining $a=0.125\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ up the hill; $T=1050$ N.

teacher_walkthrough: First treat the car and trailer together as one combined system. The total mass is $M = 1200 + 800 = 2000\text{ kg}$.

Calculate all forces dragging the combined system backwards down the incline: total air resistance ($150 + 100 = 250\text{ N}$) plus the component of gravity ($Mg\sin\theta$):
$$F_{\text{opposing}} = 250 + 2000(10)(0.1) = 250 + 2000 = 2250\text{ N}$$

Find the net force acting on the whole vehicle by subtracting opposing forces from the 2500 N driving force:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 2500 - 2250 = 250\text{ N}$$

Use Newton's second law ($F_{\text{net}} = Ma$) and divide by 2000 to find acceleration $a$:
$$250 = 2000 \times a \implies a = \frac{250}{2000} = \frac{1}{8} = 0.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Now isolate the 800 kg trailer. Cable tension $T$ pulls it forward, while its 100 N resistance and slope weight component drag it back:
$$T - 100 - 800(10)(0.1) = 800 \times a$$

Simplify the arithmetic and solve for tension $T$:
$$T - 100 - 800 = 800(0.125)$$
$$T - 900 = 100 \implies T = 100 + 900 + 50 = 1050\text{ N}$$

hints: When the engine is switched off, the driving force is $0$. Find the new deceleration of the system.
Use $v = u + at$ with $u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v = 0$ to find the time to come to rest.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law to the combined system after the driving force is cut off ($F_D = 0$):
$$-R_{\text{total}} - Mg\sin\theta = Ma$$
$$-250 - 2000(10)(0.1) = 2000a \implies -2250 = 2000a \implies a = -1.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT relation $v = u + at$ to find the time $t$ until the vehicles stop ($v = 0$):
$$0 = 30 + (-1.125)t \implies 1.125t = 30$$
$$t = \frac{30}{1.125} = \frac{80}{3} \approx 26.7\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
When the car engine stops, the driving force drops to zero ($F_D = 0$). Only the 250 N resistance and 2000 N backward slope gravity act on the 2000 kg system:
$$F_{\text{net}} = -250 - 2000 = -2250\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law to find the deceleration of the vehicle:
$$-2250 = 2000 \times a \implies a = -\frac{2250}{2000} = -1.125\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Use the SUVAT relation connecting initial speed, final speed, acceleration, and time ($v = u + at$):
$$0 = 30 + (-1.125)t$$

Add $1.125t$ to both sides and divide by $1.125$ to isolate time $t$:
$$1.125t = 30 \implies t = \frac{30}{1.125} = \frac{30000}{1125} = \frac{80}{3} \approx 26.7\text{ seconds}$$
